input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 19. the team planned Rd1 (rook_a1), but bishop_f1 (greed) sent Bxe4 instead, and that move was played, costing 191 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 6. the team planned g4 (pawn_g2), but pawn_g2 (amnesia) sent g3 instead, and that move was played, costing 8 centipawns.
- On move 10. the team planned Rh2 (rook_h1), but knight_g1 (greed) sent Ndxb5 instead, and that move was played, costing 88 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send your piece's move only if you are the piece named in the plan and the move matches it exactly; if the plan names another piece, stay silent, and do not deviate for threats or captures unless the team has explicitly approved the change in chat.
- Before sending any move, post it in chat and wait for the plan-named piece to confirm the exact move; if your piece is not named in the plan, send nothing, even when it can capture material or is attacked, and if your piece is named, send only the exact planned move, double-checking the move text against the plan before sending.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, check that the exact move and your piece's name appear in the latest plan in chat; if they do not match, send nothing, and if you think the plan is wrong (a threat or a capture), post that in chat and let the team agree on a new plan instead of acting alone.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
